newsitem.title: SPAIN: ATHLETICS-SOTOMAYOR SOARS BACK TO TOP FORM.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-SOTOMAYOR SOARS BACK TO TOP FORM.

text.p: Javier Sotomayor of Cuba sprang back to top form on Monday at the scene of his high jump world record four years ago.
Sotomayor produced his best performance since February last year with a clearence of 2.34 metres at the Salamanca international meeting.
The soaring effort came on his first attempt at the height and is the second best mark in the world this year.
The Cuban, who was the 1991 and 1993 world champion, set the world best of 2.45 metres at the corresponding meeting in 1993.
Sotomayor has endured knee and ankle operations since he limped away from the Olympic final last August when he could only finish 11th.
"I'm now about 97 percent recovered. After this performance I am very encouraged," said Sotomayor.
The athletics track in the Spanish city is now named after Sotomayor and it was fitting that the Cuban was named "man of the meeting".
Other impressive performers included American long jumper Eric Walder with a wind-assited 8.27 metres.
Burundi's Venuste Niyangabo, the Olympic 5,000 metres champion, tuned up for the world championships in Athens next month with an easy victory over 1,500 metres in three minutes 34.70 seconds.
Niyangabo has said he will contest the metric mile at the world championships.
